items.title: Chink Martin Interview, 1966-10-19
items.q: When he was learning us, he had about, let's see, it was Mossoy and King, myself. There was three of us.

ctx.x: Dr. Tishner's antiseptic. Well, if you get them to think about it, they can improve, I think.

Dr. Tishner's antiseptic. Well, they could improve. But could you knock it in their head to keep tempo? Dr. Tishner's antiseptic. No. That would be less. That's something that you can't learn a poison. It's got to come from under your heart. Dr. Tishner's antiseptic. In other words, you've got to have that feeling. If you haven't got that feeling, nothing happens. Now, I'll show you what I mean about that. We're coming right back to this old professor, Francisco Quinones. When he was learning us, he had about,…

That was the final. Well, from those early days then, they had, did they have white musicians playing what today we could have called early jazz? They had white musicians. The boys? At the turn of the century now we're talking about, they had white musicians playing jazz then. Now what were they called?
